memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: all the towns on the plateau and the entire realm of Sihon king of the Amorites, who ruled at Heshbon. Moses had defeated him and the Midianite chiefs, Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur and Reba—princes allied with Sihon—who lived in that country. In addition to those slain in battle, the Israelites had put to the sword Balaam son of Beor, who practiced divination. The boundary of the Reubenites was the bank of the Jordan. These towns and their villages were the inheritance of the Reubenites, according to their clans - Josh 13:21-23 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
Tucked into this record of Reuben's territory is a striking name: Balaam son of Beor, who practised divination. Balaam was the prophet-for-hire whom Israel's enemies had paid to curse God's people. He could not curse them — God turned his words into blessing — but he later schemed to lead Israel into sin through temptation (Num 31:16). Here we read that Balaam met his end among the slain.

Balaam is a sobering figure. He knew the true God, spoke real prophecies, and yet his heart was set on reward and compromise. The New Testament holds him up as a warning against those who love the wages of wickedness (2 Pet 2:15). It is possible to have great spiritual knowledge and still be far from God in the heart. Balaam is proof that gifting is not the same as godliness.

But there is deep comfort here too. The one hired to curse God's people could not do it, and in the end his schemes failed utterly. No curse, no scheme, no enemy could undo God's blessing on His people. That is our security as well. In Christ, nothing and no one can bring a lasting charge against those God has justified (Rom 8:33-34). The Balaams of this world may plot, but the blessing of God on His people cannot be reversed.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
- Does Balaam warn you that spiritual knowledge is not the same as a heart set on God?
- Where might you be tempted, like Balaam, by reward or compromise?
- How does it comfort you that no curse or scheme can undo God's blessing on His people?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, guard my heart from loving reward more than loving You. Thank You that no scheme of the enemy can reverse the blessing You have spoken over Your people in Christ. Amen.
